scope: Full 117-signal ASIC to XC7A100T CSG324 to XEM8310 board
status_definition: Open means not resolved by accepted design evidence. Known implementation gaps are recorded separately; owner roles are proposed, not accepted assignments.

items.title: ASIC electrical limits
items.known: The accepted count is 117. Slides 13–14 and 25–28 show recording/control directions: CLK_IN, resets, SPI L/R/CLK/LATCH and stimulation controls go FPGA to ASIC; CLK_OUT, DATA, READ and SYNC return to FPGA. The underlying table lists 1.5 V nominal supply; that row is hidden by an overlay in the visible slides.
items.uncertainty: Guaranteed logic thresholds, output drive, load/leakage, absolute limits and powered-off behavior are absent for the full interface. AC_IN and IMP_TST still lack confirmed functions and directions. A nominal supply is not a guaranteed I/O specification.
items.closure: Obtain a versioned ASIC pad specification or designer-approved table for all signal classes; compare limits against the selected FPGA standard and power states.

items.title: ASIC timing and sample format
items.known: Slides 15–17 show 32 MHz recording, 1,024 clocks/frame, 16 READ groups, and 16 zero clocks plus 48 payload clocks/group. Samples are bit-interleaved A1 bit 0, A2 bit 0, A3 bit 0, A4 bit 0 through bit 11. Slide 26 specifies four 3-bit DR suffix fields and shows a stream ending at bit 2124.
items.uncertainty: Capture edge, setup/hold, delay/skew/jitter limits, ADC numeric coding and pause/restart behavior remain unqualified. The channel table duplicates A49/A57 and omits A50/A59. Full SPI packing is missing. Stimulation timing conflicts: 31.25 us, 32 us/step and 60 kHz; the <200 Hz limit also conflicts with a 5 ms example.
items.closure: Obtain a corrected versioned channel map, ADC coding, full SPI serializer/workbook and stimulation timing; approve guaranteed pad timing, then constrain and verify capture against an accepted model and measured waveforms.

items.title: Which physical chip uses each signal
items.proposed_owner: ASIC/carrier and routing designers + FPGA design
items.known: The 117 names have proposed contacts across two 60-contact connectors. The tutorial describes eight serial DATA outputs per ASIC and an illustrative DATA1 channel map with duplicate/missing labels.
items.uncertainty: ASIC1–8 and BOARD1–4 are logical slots; the actual stimulation-chip, non-stimulation board, clock and SPI-sharing groups are not mapped end to end.
items.closure: Produce matching ASIC pad → carrier → routing board → mezzanine → FPGA tables, with direction and shared-net loading; review both mating sides.

items.title: Inactive states during startup and faults
items.known: Slides 27–28 depict SPI load, assert STIM_EN, pulse STIM_START, then STIM_CHB after 64 STIM_CLK cycles. Chip_Reset and FE_RESET functions are described. PUDC_B is pulled high; the templates disable bias on unused pins after configuration.
items.uncertainty: Asserted reset polarity, pulse width/settling, drive ownership and safe preconfiguration, brownout and reprogramming states remain unspecified. Positive-going normal-operation drawings do not approve default bias or fault interlocks; the listed <1.5 ms reset time is not a digital pulse-width specification.
items.closure: Approve a state table for every shared control and power state, implement required bias/interlocks, and test power-order and configuration-failure cases.

items.title: ASIC-board power and return paths
items.proposed_owner: ASIC/routing power designer + system power design
items.known: The 120 numbered mezzanine contacts contain 117 signals plus three reserves; ground blades are separate. The tutorial gives about 17.24 uW/channel for recording, excluding LDOs, and ±10 V stimulation compliance; neither defines the assembly power tree.
items.uncertainty: ASIC analog/digital/stimulation supplies, their source, return currents and any separate power connector are not allocated in this interface. The FPGA 1.5 V I/O rail is not an approved ASIC power supply.
items.closure: Define the complete assembly power tree and current budget; specify which board supplies every ASIC rail and its return, including powered-off cases.

items.title: Exact FPGA ordering code
items.known: XC7A100T in 15 × 15 mm CSG324 is selected; the proposed core supply is approximately 1.0 V.
items.uncertainty: Speed and temperature grades are unselected. A low-voltage -1LI device is not interchangeable with the present core supply, and link timing depends on grade.
items.closure: Freeze the full purchasable order code, check every supply limit and timing target, and use that exact part in the Vivado project and BOM.

items.title: Legal FPGA pin and clock allocation
items.known: The 324-pin inventory matches AMD; 150 pads are in the 1.5 V banks, with 12 P-side clock groups and four complete bank-16 differential pairs.
items.uncertainty: Capacity does not prove placement legality. The 117 application nets, eight link pads and eight returned-clock domains have no implemented pin/timing allocation.
items.closure: Create complete XDC and HDL, check bank voltages and clock regions, constrain all interfaces and CDC, and obtain clean implementation/timing reports for the selected device.

items.title: Mezzanine mating and complete assembly fit
items.known: Two QSH-030-01-L-D-A candidates fit the 40 × 36 mm 2D study; QTH mates use a different land pattern.
items.uncertainty: Mating-board orientation, contact numbering, tolerance, board separation, component heights and support/fastening are unqualified. The documented H-dimension ambiguity remains open.
items.closure: Resolve the manufacturer drawing ambiguity; build both mating PCB footprints with exact order codes, check pin-1 continuity and full 3D/tolerance/assembly clearance.

items.title: Micro-HDMI part, edge and cable construction
items.known: J4 carries a custom non-HDMI interface. Its saved edge datum is 0.70 mm inside the actual board edge.
items.uncertainty: Exact order code, plug fit, approved copper-edge clearance, wire mapping, shield/return construction, current rating and cable length qualification are not frozen.
items.closure: Choose a specific connector and custom cable; reconcile its current drawing with the PCB edge, verify continuity/orientation, mating access and loaded cable behavior.

items.title: Actual FPGA power and temperature
items.known: The rail allocations and tolerance calculations are provisional; no workload-based power estimate or assembled-board measurement exists.
items.uncertainty: Worst-case rail current, converter efficiency/stability, voltage droop and device/inductor temperature are unknown at the real acquisition workload and operating environment.
items.closure: Complete a workload/activity-based power model, allocate rail margins and capacitor bias/temperature effects, then test load steps, rails and thermal rise on the completed assembly.

items.title: Power-entry protection and power ordering
items.known: Protected 12 V, 0.60 A continuous and a cable up to 0.30 m are design proposals; the proposed protection and damping are not installed.
items.uncertainty: Source tolerances, inrush, current limiting, hot-plug overshoot, ESD, shutdown order and back-powering across independently powered boards are unqualified.
items.closure: Implement a complete protected source/entry and power-state design with actual cable/load values, then verify startup, faults, cable events and power loss against component limits.

items.title: XEM8310 contacts and voltage/ready contract
items.known: XEM8310 is an FPGA/USB receiver module. Bank64 VIO1 defaults to 1.0 V; BOARD_READY is initialization status, not continuous rail monitoring.
items.uncertainty: Exact module contacts, bank selection, stored VIO settings, target-JTAG GPIOs and startup/loss-of-power interlock are not implemented.
items.closure: Freeze the carrier schematic and pin map; verify stored voltages and compatible I/O standards, explicit training/readiness and behavior through reconfiguration and power loss.

items.title: LVDS and JTAG electrical margins
items.known: A direct DC LVDS connection lacks guaranteed positive ground-offset allowance at published corners; this is not proof every cable fails.
items.uncertainty: Receiver bias/termination or AC coupling, per-lane balance, return-path offset, jitter/skew and static JTAG levels/timing are not qualified.
items.closure: Choose and implement the receiver network and JTAG voltage scheme; analyze worst-case levels and transients, then measure link eye/error margin and JTAG over the actual cable.

items.title: Data packing, USB boundaries and control protocol
items.known: Each READ group has 16 zero clocks followed by 48 payload clocks (25% padding), carrying interleaved 12-bit samples needing deinterleaving. Three proposed 800 Mbit/s lanes provide 240 MB/s after 8b/10b; packed 12-bit samples fit the arithmetic budget, 16-bit sample padding does not.
items.uncertainty: ADC coding, complete SPI serialization and corrected stimulation timing remain unapproved. Lane alignment, encoding, frame/CRC metadata, USB boundaries, commands and remote programming have no implemented contract. The proposed 6,165-byte frame does not itself meet 32-bit word / 16-byte USB boundaries.
items.closure: Specify continuous repacking or padding/aggregation, byte/channel order, lane training and command handling; simulate and verify the exact wire-to-USB-to-file format.

items.title: Buffering and data loss during host stalls
items.known: The proposed four LVDS pairs all travel toward the receiver. USB throttling alone does not stop incoming ASIC data. At the proposed framed rate, a 100 ms no-drain interval needs about 19.27 MB; this is arithmetic, not tested buffering.
items.uncertainty: Allowed host stall, usable buffer depth/bandwidth, reverse flow control, and overrun/recovery policy are undefined. The tutorial starts recording with CLK_IN but does not authorize stopping or restarting it as lossless backpressure.
items.closure: Set a bounded stall requirement; size and implement buffering with sustained read/write bandwidth, define loss/backpressure policy, and stress-test a stalled host with sequence/error counters.

items.title: Manufacturing process and final minimum size
items.known: All three studies have 40 × 36 mm outlines and six copper layers; existing physical checks pass their configured rules.
items.uncertainty: No approved dielectric stackup, impedance, full BGA escape, fabrication/assembly process, final BOM or integrated smallest board exists.
items.closure: Select an achievable fabricator stackup/process, integrate all required circuits/connectors, route and review SI/PI/DFM and assembly tolerances; derive the final outline from that completed design.

items.title: Boot recovery and test access without headers
items.known: Optional LED, debug headers and test points are removed. The older blink procedure is legacy-only; compact revisions have different configuration voltages. Tutorial ASIC reset functions do not define this compact FPGA board’s bring-up sequence.
items.uncertainty: No matching validated build, power-on procedure, fixture access plan or demonstrated flash brownout/reset/recovery exists for either compact revision.
items.closure: Create a revision-specific HDL/XDC/build and test procedure, select supported flash programming, identify accessible existing pads/J4, and verify JTAG, rail ramps, clock and cold-boot recovery.

items.title: Measured full-system operation
items.known: No assembled instance of this design has demonstrated power-up or acquisition; earlier ECP5 tests concern another system.
items.uncertainty: Functional correctness, all-channel mapping, sustained throughput to disk, error rate, thermal margin and repeatable recovery remain unmeasured. The intended PC/storage and required recording duration are not fixed; compact framing produces about 693.56 GB/hour before storage overhead.
items.closure: After engineering closure, run a documented prototype acceptance plan with known channel patterns and real ASIC data, power cycling, fault recovery and sustained disk capture with error counters.

known_gaps.title: No single integrated full-board design
known_gaps.detail: The core, rail revision and mezzanine fit are separate. Integrate the selected rails, both mezzanines and required headboard circuitry into one complete headboard schematic/PCB; provide a matching separate carrier/cable interface design.

known_gaps.title: Application pins are unassigned
known_gaps.detail: Both schematics have 203 unassigned FPGA user I/O and eight unassigned J4 data contacts. The mezzanine study has 120 unassigned numbered contacts; the 117 signal CSV is only a proposal.

known_gaps.title: Assigned copper is unfinished
known_gaps.detail: Third-pass native DRC records 139 missing items in the core, 347 in the rail revision and 383 in the placement study. These counts exclude unassigned application signals.

known_gaps.title: Full firmware and receiver are not implemented
known_gaps.detail: No complete application HDL/XDC, carrier, packet/USB path or matched compact-board build has been validated.

known_gaps.title: Manufacturing outputs are not released
known_gaps.detail: The exact BOM, stackup, Gerbers, drills and assembly files have not been released from one completed reviewed design.

known_gaps.title: Prototype acceptance has not happened
known_gaps.detail: No operating hardware evidence exists for these compact revisions. File checks and repeated reviews cannot replace measured acceptance.

external_inputs.title: Actual ASIC and mating-board specification
external_inputs.needed: ASIC revision and pad limits, corrected channel map and stimulation timing, complete SPI workbook/serializer and inactive states; physical eight-chip/group map; actual routing-board power and mating CAD. Tutorial framing and functional directions are now documented. A designer-approved specification or marked-up schematic can resolve the remaining points.

external_inputs.title: Operating and recording requirements
external_inputs.needed: Required acquisition/stimulation modes and command latency, maximum ambient/enclosure, intended recording duration, and permitted behavior when the PC stalls or disconnects. The actual PC/USB/storage is needed for final qualification.
external_inputs.owner: System/lab owner; engineering can continue with explicit provisional targets

external_inputs.title: Already-purchased parts, only if applicable
external_inputs.needed: Exact FPGA marking/order code if already purchased or mandated; otherwise engineering can select and qualify the standard-voltage part.

engineering_delegated: Power setup, exact pin choices, cable/component selection, receiver circuitry and firmware remain engineering tasks; the user is not being asked to design them.

slide_followup.scope: All 28 original slides, visual and embedded-media review; no native CAD changes or uncertainty closures
